source.title: What Do Compressed Deep Neural Networks Forget
source.authors: Sara Hooker; Aaron C. Courville; Gregory Clark; Y. Dauphin; Andrea Frome

page_placements.theme: Pruning and compression have method-dependent costs and benefits

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies pruning and quantization and reports changes in test accuracy, exemplar-level performance, and robustness. These results qualify the role of capacity and compression, but do not test random-label memorization or the listed optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or generalization-measure claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports top-line accuracy, class-level changes, PIE performance, and shifted-data performance for pruned or quantized classifiers. It does not measure train-versus-test error gaps or whether networks fit random labels. Human attribute comparisons describe PIE/non-PIE image properties, not changes to model generalization.
record.test_reason: The study measures pruning and quantization effects, which test none of V1–V8. Pruning weights is neither widening networks past interpolation (V2) nor removing memorized training examples and retraining (V8). Section 4 discusses and cites V8's source, but supplies no direct test of that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: aggregate accuracy can conceal disproportionate compression effects on particular classes and atypical examples, and pruning increases sensitivity to corruptions and natural adversarial images, especially at high sparsity. The proposed role of excess capacity in representing rare examples is an interpretation, not a direct memorization-removal experiment.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains standard image classifiers and progressively prunes them or applies post-training quantization; its question is compression's disaggregated impact, not the listed memorization/generalization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/task complexity, pruning fraction, compression method, and corruption type change the reported impact. Quantization shows fewer significantly affected ImageNet classes than aggressive pruning; ImageNet-C effects vary by corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Compression can leave aggregate accuracy similar while disproportionately changing class recall. ImageNet has 68, 170, 372 and 637 significantly impacted classes at 30%, 50%, 70% and 90% pruning, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning and quantization have non-uniform effects across classes, with stronger disparate impact at high pruning levels.

fits_no_version.finding: PIEs are defined by disagreement between compressed and uncompressed model populations. Uncompressed models also classify these selected test examples poorly; no training-example removal or retraining is performed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Examples whose predictions change under pruning tend to be difficult even for uncompressed classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning reduces relative accuracy on ImageNet-C and ImageNet-A, with greater reductions at higher sparsity and substantial variation across corruptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning can amplify sensitivity to natural image corruptions and natural adversarial examples.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code is publicly available here, but supplies no URL)
record.problems: The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the tabulated means; robustness averages use five independently trained models. The flattened CIFAR-10 table does not clearly align all class-count values to pruning fractions. The robustness results concern shifted test data, outside the claim's same-distribution scope.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional ImageNet-C corruption types and pruning levels in Appendix Table 3 and Figure 7, plus ImageNet-A pruning levels in Appendix Table 8; only representative corruption conditions and the key increasing-pruning endpoints are retained under the 60-row cap. Additional PIE counts by dataset/pruning level and human-study attribute percentages are omitted because these do not directly test a listed version; relevant summary findings are noted under fits_no_version. Figure 4/7 values without recoverable numerical descriptions were not transcribed.

untested.parts: Joint random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations of the training recipe.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Influence-based memorization identification, removal of training examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed version. This does not negate the compression effects themselves. Table alignment errors affect ImageNet class and PIE counts and CIFAR-10 subset results. Table 3's caption states 50 models, whereas Appendix D states five models per robustness condition; the source is inconsistent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under standard training.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error across width.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout intervention and its effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization measures tracking train-test gaps.
Removing examples identified as memorized and measuring retrained test accuracy.

relation.reason: Section 4 discusses memorization benefiting generalization and cites Feldman and Zhang, without directly testing V8 or using its finding as an experimental tool.

tranche.reason: Compression's effects on class recall, exemplar predictions and robustness do not test V1–V8. Weight pruning does not measure widening beyond interpolation or removing memorized training examples and retraining.

source_check.notes: Significantly impacted classes include both positive and negative relative recall changes, controlling for overall accuracy changes. The supplied text is arXiv v3, dated September 2021.
